new_rows.claim: The T312 parallel 4×4 fixpoint was measured on an Apple M5 Max (6P+12E, 48 GB LPDDR5). All artifacts from N∈{1,2,4,6,12,16} threads are byte-identical to the T310 serial reference (SHA-256 0c3366f07fb33c6f2838ead48ad3080b64dbe55935b87af4f140d81a29e4e15a). Speedup curve: N=1 (Gauss-Seidel, 31 sweeps) 3,965s baseline → N=2 (Jacobi, 59 sweeps) 4,095s (0.97×, no speedup — Jacobi overhead dominates) → N=4 2,489s (1.59×) → N=6 1,917s (2.07×) → N=12 1,371s (2.89×) → N=16 1,361s (2.91×). The curve flattens at N=12: adding 4 more threads (+33%) yields 0.7% improvement, consistent with memory-bandwidth saturation on a ~3 GB/sweep hash-map workload. Peak RSS is stable at 3,887±1 MB across all thread counts. Binary: weizigo-oracle-v2-build SHA-256 efcec15905790eb0df3ee33b4dc90c1035c6453b48d1c4f738e8c4a4e57a5526 (built from b3d0209).

notes:
T314 — PARALLEL FIXPOINT MEASUREMENT.

=== WHAT I DID ===
1. Measured the speedup curve for the T312 parallel fixpoint on an Apple M5 Max (6 P-cores + 12 E-cores, 48 GB LPDDR5). Six rows: threads = 1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 16 — same binary, same input, sequential runs under tools/runner (never two concurrently). Binary snapshotted to /tmp/weizigo/t314-snapshot/weizigo-oracle-v2-build (SHA-256 efcec15905790eb0df3ee33b4dc90c1035c6453b48d1c4f738e8c4a4e57a5526).

2. N=1 uses the serial Gauss-Seidel path (31 sweeps, 3,965s wall). N≥2 uses parallel Jacobi (59 sweeps, thread-count-independent). Root values identical across all runs: (empty,B) L=1 H=16, (empty,W) L=-16 H=-1.

3. Bit-identity: Every artifact (v03 through v09) is byte-identical to the T310 serial reference (SHA-256 0c3366f07fb33c6f2838ead48ad3080b64dbe55935b87af4f140d81a29e4e15a). This is the strongest result: T312's hypothesis that group ordering from hash-map iteration order might differ is falsified — the artifact writer is deterministic regardless of thread count. Parallelism costs nothing in reproducibility.

=== SPEEDUP CURVE ===
Threads  Wall(s)   RSS(MB)  Sweeps  CPU(s)    CPU/Wall  Speedup
1 (GS)   3,965.4   3,886    31      3,962.8   1.00×     1.00×
2        4,094.6   3,887    59      6,868.5   1.68×     0.97×
4        2,488.5   3,887    59      6,946.9   2.79×     1.59×
6        1,917.0   3,887    59      7,042.7   3.67×     2.07×
12       1,371.4   3,888    59      7,453.2   5.43×     2.89×
16       1,361.3   3,888    59      9,366.0   6.88×     2.91×

=== FLATTENING ===
The curve flattens at N=12 (2.89×). N=16 adds 4 more E-cores (+33% threads) for only 0.7% improvement (2.91×). This is the memory-bandwidth saturation signature: 18 cores share one LPDDR5 memory bus, and the fixpoint reads ~3 GB per sweep (compact_list 792 MB + hash map ~1.6 GB + L/H tables ~400 MB) through random-access hash map lookups. Peak RSS is constant at ~3,887 MB regardless of thread count, confirming T312's bounded per-thread memory claim.

=== N=2 SLOWER THAN N=1 ===
This is expected: N=1 uses Gauss-Seidel (in-place updates, 31 sweeps), N≥2 uses Jacobi (reads from previous sweep, 59 sweeps). At N=2 the Jacobi sweep-count penalty (~1.9×) outweighs the parallelism gain (~2× max). Break-even is between N=2 and N=4.

=== BIT-IDENTITY ===
All six artifacts are byte-identical to T310's serial reference. T312's hypothesis that group ordering from hash-map iteration order might cause byte differences is FALSIFIED — the artifact writer is deterministic. The artifact carries no build stamp, thread count, or timing information that could perturb the bytes. This also confirms that T264's version stamping does not reach the artifact bytes (already established by T310; now confirmed across the parallel/serial boundary).

=== EXP6_HCHAIN_AUDIT DUPLICATION ===
Confirmed: src/exp6_hchain_audit.zig:1100 has its own run_fixpoint_4x4() with no num_threads parameter — a third copy of the fixpoint, untouched by T312. This is the pre-T312 serial-only code. RECOMMENDATION: Add a header comment at line 1100 stating "DUPLICATE of exp6_solve.zig run_fixpoint_4x4 — serial-only, not updated for T312 parallelism. Under the duplication-as-oracle doctrine this is an asset, but label it so readers do not assume it shares T312's parallelism." Do NOT merge them — a redundant implementation is a cross-check, not a defect.

=== WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH ===
- Memory bandwidth during the run (beyond the inference from the flattening shape). The host has no hardware performance counters accessible without sudo.
- Whether the hash map iteration order is truly deterministic or accidentally stable across these 6 runs. A future change to the hash map implementation (e.g., random seeding) could break reproducibility even though this measurement shows it holds today.
- N=18 (all cores). The brief's core budget is 9–16 (50–90% of 18), so N=18 is out of scope.

=== WHAT I NOTICED BUT DID NOT ACT ON ===
- zig build test is non-deterministic: first run 390/393 passed, second run 393/393 passed but 1 build step failed, third run all green. This is pre-existing (present at b3d0209 before T314 started).
- v03 artifact was created by an accidentally-aborted test run (head -20 closing the pipe caused SIGPIPE mid-write, but the artifact was already flushed). Its SHA-256 also matches — an unintentional third serial reproduction.
- The binary does not emit [progress] markers, so the runner's --progress-timeout 7200 acts as a wall-clock watchdog (same as T310). Adding [progress] markers per sweep would enable tighter progress-timeout values.
